why: I checked every claim against the repository files and they all hold. bin/greet.js picks the first argument that doesn't start with `--`, so "Any argument starting with `--` is silently dropped" is true, and `--shout Bob` prints `Hello, Bob!` and exits 0. The usage message goes to stderr with exit 2, as the no-name case says. docs/index.md documents only `node bin/greet.js <name>`. pages.yml publishes `docs` on every push to main, and the README gives the URL https://o.github.io/greet-cli/. src/greet.js exports `greeting(name)`, test/ exists and package.json defines `npm test`. The --shout option is new, which is what the issue asks for. The outcome writes "greet --shout <name>" even though package.json has no bin entry. That is just shorthand: the CLI's own usage text says `greet <name>`, and every testable line uses `node bin/greet.js`. Nothing in the issue invents a file, function or behavior.
